Here's a proposed structure for `misc/`, plus a plan to fix `utils/` (I need one more input from you to finish that part — details below).

## Folder map — `misc/` breakdown

| Current content | New home | Disposition |
|---|---|---|
| Config templates | `config/templates/` | Kept — versioned reference |
| One-off migration scripts | `scripts/migrations/` | Kept, append-only — historical/audit trail, never edited after merge |
| Archived compliance reports | `compliance/archive/` (or `docs/compliance/archive/` if you already have a `docs/` root) | Archived — retention-governed, don't delete without compliance sign-off |
| Shared helpers used by 2 services | `packages/shared/` (or `libs/shared/` if you don't use a monorepo package convention) | Kept — versioned code, needs a named owner since two services depend on it |
| Old meeting notes | Not the repo — move to your wiki/drive | N/A — meeting notes aren't build artifacts; recommend exporting and deleting from the repo |

Each of these maps to a single reason-to-change (config changes together, migrations are immutable history, compliance reports are retention records, shared code changes when the shared contract changes), so they're real folders, not junk drawers.

## `utils/` — needs one more thing from you

30 "unrelated helper files" is exactly the junk-drawer failure this skill flags — grouping by "is a helper" isn't a real category, it has no single reason to change. To split it correctly I need to know what the files actually do and who consumes them, not just that they're miscellaneous. Could you share a quick list of filenames with a one-line purpose each (or just paste `ls utils/`)? I'll bucket them by consuming domain — e.g. `libs/formatting/`, `libs/validation/`, `libs/http/` — rather than by "type of util."

## Naming / depth / single-source check

- ✅ All proposed paths lowercase, hyphen-separated, ≤3 levels deep
- ✅ No `misc`, `utils`, `stuff`, `tmp` names anywhere in the new tree
- ✅ Each folder maps to exactly one WBS-like piece or disposition rule — no idea has two homes
- ⚠️ `packages/shared/` needs an owner assigned (two services depend on it — undocumented shared code is how these drawers form in the first place)

## Escalation flag

This changes your top-level repo convention (`misc`/`utils` → `config`/`scripts`/`compliance`/`packages`), which affects everyone committing to the repo. I'd confirm the new top-level names with the team/owner before merging, rather than restructuring unilaterally — happy to draft the README stubs for each new folder once the layout is agreed.
